## Acceptance Criteria

REQ-02 is met by the committed, re-runnable self-test evidence. REQ-03 is met structurally: `.jit/gates.toml` registers the three-checker aggregate script.

REQ-01 is not met. The default gate footprint now resolves exclusively to `[documentation].permanent_paths`, currently `docs/`. It omits the plan’s adopter-facing root/component documents: `README.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `mcp-server/README.md`, and `web/README.md`.

## Architecture and Separation of Concerns

No Rust architecture boundaries were changed. The implementation remains confined to scripts, documentation, gate configuration, and issue metadata.

## Functional Paradigm

The shell and embedded Python use pragmatic imperative filesystem/process handling. No blocking functional-style issue was identified.

## Correctness and Invariants

The aggregate script preserves child finding versus environment-error semantics. Projection self-testing remains isolated in a disposable clone.

However, the no-argument gate no longer checks its declared full adopter-documentation surface. At [scripts/docs-mechanical.sh](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/scripts/docs-mechanical.sh:62), only `permanent_paths` are collected. This contradicts both the script’s own lines 21–28 and the gate description at `.jit/gates.toml:151`.

No issue-state, event-log, transition, assignee, label, PID, atomic-write, or unsafe Rust implementation changed.

## Safety

No unsafe code was introduced. The self-test does not mutate the active repository worktree or index.

## Testing

The supplied evidence records all six clean/seeded self-test assertions passing and shellcheck succeeding. No failed test result appears in the latest test evidence.

Per instruction, I did not run the Rust test suite. I ran the required validator:

`✓ Repository validation passed`

Shell syntax validation and `git diff --check` also passed.

## Error Handling

The aggregate script correctly maps findings to exit code 1 and environment or unexpected errors to exit code 2. No new error-handling defect was found.

## CLI Contract

No user-facing CLI command was added or changed. The universal `--json` requirement is not applicable to repository gate scripts.

## Documentation

The current footprint documentation is internally contradictory. Lines 21–28 still claim the default includes repository-root and immediate-subdirectory Markdown, while the implementation and later comment say only configured permanent roots are included.

More importantly, `.jit/gates.toml` still describes a no-argument run as checking the “full adopter doc surface,” which the implementation no longer does.

## Prior Review Feedback

The latest prior finding—the hardcoded depth cutoff—was removed. The replacement introduces a broader coverage regression: all adopter-facing documents outside `docs/` are now omitted from automatic gate runs.

Earlier citation, reference-link, destructive-cleanup, execution-evidence, and aggregate-exit-status findings remain resolved under the amended owner-approved criteria.

## JIT Issue Management

The prerequisite `c939d0b6` is complete and there are no unmet dependencies. `./scripts/jit-validate.sh` passes.

## Findings

1. **F1 — High:** The no-argument `docs-mechanical` gate no longer covers the full adopter documentation surface. `resolve_footprint` collects only `documentation.permanent_paths` at `scripts/docs-mechanical.sh:62`, currently just `docs/`, omitting `README.md`, `INSTALL.md`, `mcp-server/README.md`, and `web/README.md` from automatic checks. This conflicts with the plan’s audited surface, the gate description, and the script’s own footprint contract; hard REQ-01 therefore remains unmet.

Total findings: 1
